assessment: The four briefed visuals are distinct and load-bearing: the sequence exposes reuse in the N=8 factorization, the butterfly binds algebra to an in-place update, the cost ledger separates structural counts from runtime, and the cell ledger makes natural and reversed layouts auditable. All four are constructed mathematical explanations; a scanned paper page would add provenance but not visible evidence for any of these claims.
scope_guardrail: Use the inherited unscaled negative-sign forward DFT and 1/N positive-sign inverse. Count direct work as N^2 complex products plus N(N-1) complex additions, radix-2 work as (N/2)log2(N) twiddle slots plus Nlog2(N) additions, and the historical mixed-radix budget as T=N sum_i r_i complex multiply-add units. Never combine those ledgers into one unnamed operation count. Natural order is k=0,...,N-1; bit/digit reversal is a storage permutation, not a new frequency axis. Actual wall-clock crossover is machine- and implementation-dependent and remains unclaimed.

Cite or link it in prose if desired, but do not use it as one of the four figures.

figures.brief_visual: Natural, bit-reversed, and mixed-radix memory-order cell grids
figures.tier_reason: The figure compares rows of unequal length, digit equations, source-to-address arrows, and an interface checklist. Responsive HTML grids with KaTeX keep every index literal and prevent the mixed-radix rule from becoming microscopic SVG prose.
figures.source_status: house component from verified index permutations; no sourced artifact
figures.embed: <Figure name="FftMemoryOrderLedger" alt="Aligned cell rows show natural order zero through seven, three-bit reversal zero four two six one five three seven, and a twelve-cell mixed-radix three-by-four layout whose destination addresses contain source indices zero three six nine one four seven ten two five eight eleven." caption="Reversed layouts are explicit storage permutations; restore natural k order before plotting or comparing spectra." />
figures.teaching_claim: Bit and digit reversal change which source index occupies each memory address, not the physical meaning of frequency bin k; the permutation is therefore part of the FFT interface contract.

exact_data.cell_semantics: each row lists the source index n held at destination address p, read left to right in increasing p
exact_data.n8_rule: p=reverse_3_bits(n); bit reversal is self-inverse for this row
exact_data.n12_digits: n=d_0+3d_1 with d_0 in {0,1,2}, d_1 in {0,1,2,3}; destination p=d_1+4d_0
exact_data.interface: a consumer requesting natural spectral order must apply the inverse permutation before associating array position p with bin k=p
